newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua unions to hold new meeting over strike.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua unions to hold new meeting over strike.

text.p: Port operators at Brazil's port of Paranagua had still not started a meeting to consider a new proposal by striking dockworkers, but both parties were scheduled to meet at 1400 local/1700 GMT, union officials said.
"The meeting hasn't begun yet, it's going to start at midday," said a spokeswoman for the port operators' union SINDOP. The union had been scheduled to hold an assembly at 1100 local.
The port authority earlier said it was confident SINDOP would approve the dockworkers' proposal, which contains a demand for a 21 percent wage increase.

All portworkers at Paranagua went on strike at midday Wednesday in support of the dockworkers, halting the loading and unloading of all cargoes including soybeans, soymeal and corn at the port's export terminal.
"The strike should end today between 1400 and 1500," a spokeswoman for the port said earlier.

An official at the dockworkers' union said the main change in the new document was an agreement to implement reductions in the size of work teams, which would increase productivity. "The main change is the reduction in teams. We have come to an agreement about this," he said.
The measure is one of a series of changes which SINDOP is demanding within the new law governing the privatization and modernization of Brazil's ports.
Both parties were due to meet at 1400 local to discuss the document, the dockworker spokesman said. Asked whether he thought the dispute would be resolved, he said, "I am always optimistic."
